problem: RL-based target-driven visual navigation (e.g. Siamese Actor-Critic) suffers from sparse rewards, needs millions of frames, and fails to generalize to unseen targets in large multi-room real-scan environments. Other baselines (SLAM, PointGoal RL) need maps, odometry or goal coordinates.
motivation: Robots should navigate to an arbitrary goal seen only through images, without map, compass, odometry or relative goal position at runtime. Photo-realistic 3D scans in simulators allow cheap generation of optimal expert trajectories, so supervised imitation can replace sample-inefficient RL.
key_idea: Imitate Dijkstra-planned expert trajectories, discretized into forward/left/right, with an MLP policy over autoencoder embeddings of a 5-frame RGBD history and an 8-image panoramic RGBD goal, plus a separate learned goal-checking classifier for stopping.
insight: An 8-image panoramic goal is the key input: 5H+8G reaches 0.9725 SR versus 0.8925 for 5H+1G and 0.8847 for 1H+1G in the ablation. Larger MLP input beat conv/LSTM and longer histories. A separate goal checker is needed because 'done' is a rare positive label in the policy data, and it costs only a little versus an oracle localizer, except in the largest environments (area1 0.575 vs 0.660 SR).
method: Autoencoder: 6-layer CNN encoder with batch norm and 6 transposed-conv decoder layers, trained per environment on 120K RGBD images, compressing 256x256x4 into a 4096-d latent
Expert data: 1cm-resolution 2D map from the mesh, Dijkstra with costmap, collision-free paths discretized into forward 0.1m / turn 10° using a 25-step look-ahead with a 20° offset threshold
Policy model: MLP on the concatenated 13x4096 embeddings (5 state frames + 8 goal images), 3 FC layers with BN+ReLU to 16-d, 3 logits, cross-entropy imitation, greedy at test time
Goal checker: dual-branch binary classifier with 1D conv over the panoramic goal embeddings and a 5120-d fused vector into an MLP; positives are within 0.1m, negatives at least 1m away

Runtime stopping: when the checker belief exceeds 0.99 the agent spins 360° and outputs done only if the average probability over the rotation exceeds 0.9; a physics-simulated collision counts as failure

setting.backbone: Per-environment trained autoencoder + MLP policy + goal-checker CNN/MLP (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Per environment: 120K autoencoder images, 3000–7000 Dijkstra expert trajectories (~700K training frames), 150K positive and 150K negative goal-checker samples; policy ~90 GPU hours
setting.observation: Egocentric RGBD (256x256) current view + 4 past frames + 8-image panoramic RGBD goal; no map/compass/odometry
setting.action_space: Low-level discrete: forward 0.1 m, turn left/right 10°, plus done from the goal checker
setting.simulator: Gibson simulator (PyBullet) with Fetch robot on Stanford2D3DS and Matterport3D scans
setting.privileged: none at test time for 'no LOC'; the 'LOC' variant uses simulator ground-truth position and goal coordinate for stopping. Trained and tested in the same scanned environments

numbers.bench: other:Stanford2D3DS/Matterport3D Gibson target-driven nav (5 envs avg)
numbers.eval_set_note: 400 random start-goal pairs per environment, unseen targets in the trained environments, averaged over 5 environments
numbers.backbone: autoencoder + MLP policy + learned goal checker
numbers.extra: success radius 0.5m; collisions count as failure; per-environment training

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; own Gibson setup. Metrics printed as fractions. Per-environment results are in Table 1 (e.g. no LOC: house2 0.9875 SR, area1 0.5750 SR); ablation in Table 3 (5H+8G SR 0.9725).
results: Averaged over 5 environments, the no-LOC pipeline reaches 0.8125 SR / 0.6614 SPL, versus RL (PPO) 0.6650 / 0.5600, SAC 0.3705 / 0.2363, RTABMap 0.2570 / 0.1746 and DFP 0.2275 / 0.1642. It uses ~700K frames versus 20M for SAC and 90 versus 300 GPU hours. Performance drops in environments with over 30 rooms.
limitations: Trained per environment and evaluated only on unseen targets in already-seen scenes; no generalization to new environments
Performance degrades in large, many-room environments (area1 SR 0.575) and only simulation is tested
The baselines PPO/DFP/RTABMap were given privileged position or goal info or different setups, so comparisons are not fully controlled
builds_on: Target-driven visual navigation (Zhu et al., Siamese Actor-Critic)
